extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing NIH grant applications (R01/R21/R03/R15/R34 and similar)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing NIH research grant applications under the 2016 FORMS‑C interim instructions, emphasizing how to organize the Research Plan and satisfy new rigor, reproducibility, biological-variables, and authentication expectations. Covers formatting, content movement between Significance and Approach, and related budget/human/animal policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH core review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Five core review criteria: SIGNIFICANCE, INVESTIGATOR(S), INNOVATION, APPROACH, and ENVIRONMENT (these core criteria will not change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will continue to score applications using these five criteria. The 2016 changes require reviewers to search for evidence of responsiveness to NIH priorities (scientific premise, rigorous experimental design, relevant biological variables, authentication of key resources) and to incorporate those observations into scoring—especially SIGNIFICANCE and APPROACH. Any new reviewer guidance (questions/comments) will inform how these criteria are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific premise (foundation of knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific premise consists of the literature (including the applicant’s own publications) and preliminary data on which the proposed research is built; reviewers will assess strengths and weaknesses of those sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific premise now belongs in the Significance subsection (moved from Approach). Discuss overall premise and then present literature & preliminary studies organized by specific aim. Briefly critique strengths and weaknesses of cited studies and preliminary data (e.g., statistical power, blinding, design flaws). Include a sentence tying each literature/data paragraph to why it justifies the related aim. Be selective in citations (favor peer‑reviewed, methodologically strong studies) and avoid citing reviews unless appropriate. Discussion of strengths/weaknesses will influence the SIGNIFICANCE score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous experimental design for robust and unbiased results
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate strict application of the scientific method in experimental design, methodology, analysis, interpretation, and reporting to ensure robustness and lack of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address rigorous design in the Research Design sub-subsection of Approach (per‑aim Research Design). Include elements such as randomization, blinding, sample size estimation, data handling, and appropriate statistical methods. Consider adding statistical/design expertise to the team. Describe implementation (not just theory); adherence to Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) principles is recommended. Pilot/discipline resources and external materials may be cited; NIH may add reviewers with statistical/design expertise to study sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of relevant biological variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must consider biological variables (examples: sex, age, weight, health status, species/strain, diet, race/ethnicity) that could cause variation in results; sex is specifically emphasized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each proposed experiment, describe whether both sexes will be included and how sex (and other relevant variables) will be accounted for (e.g., stratified randomization, disaggregation of data, separate analysis, interpretation of sex-specific effects). If proposing single-sex studies or excluding other variables, provide strong justification. For cell lines, report sex karyotype where feasible. This consideration will affect the APPROACH score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide an authentication plan for any key resource (e.g., cell lines, specialty chemicals, antibodies, other biologics) that is critical to the research and could cause inter-lab variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentication procedures should be described in a separate one‑page attachment titled "Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources" and uploaded as a PDF to the R&R Other Project Information Other Attachments (this attachment does not count toward Research Strategy page limits). Describe acquisition (e.g., reputable source like ATCC), maintenance (freeze‑backs, working vials, frequency of re‑acquisition to avoid drift), and tests (e.g., endotoxin testing for FBS). Cite accepted standards if followed. Reviewers will rate authentication as Acceptable or Unacceptable (not part of Overall Impact score), and any Unacceptable finding must be resolved before award. Results of authentication are not required as preliminary data and external authentication is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance subsection — purposes and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Significance subsection must (i) justify the need for the proposed work, (ii) establish the scientific premise (including critique of literature and preliminary data), and (iii) state the NIH‑relevant expected impact of the contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended substructure: an introductory paragraph under "Significance:" that substantiates the problem (with citations/statistical detail), then a "Scientific Premise:" section with (a) Overall Scientific Premise and (b) Scientific Premise for Aim #1 (Literature & Preliminary Results), Aim #2, Aim #3 (if applicable), followed by "Significance of Expected Research Contribution." Keep writing succinct to stay within Research Strategy page limits. In the introductory paragraph, briefly portray relevance to the FOA/IC mission and discuss strengths/weaknesses of cited works constructively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for Research Strategy and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims and Research Strategy format changes; page limits remain the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific Aims: limited to 1 page. Research Strategy: limited to 12 pages for R01/R15/R34 and 6 pages for R03/R21. Literature review and preliminary studies have been moved to the Significance subsection (expand Significance, shorten Approach accordingly). Use succinct organization and selective citation to stay within page limits; follow the recommended format to avoid redundant presentation of data/citations across aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and presentation of supporting literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Select highly relevant, peer‑reviewed publications with strong experimental and reporting practices to support the scientific premise; avoid excessive citations and review articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be extremely judicious—include only papers that informed your thinking and that have few methodological weaknesses. If including a paper with significant weaknesses, explicitly explain why those weaknesses do not undermine its use or how you will mitigate them. End each literature paragraph with a sentence stating why the cited work justifies the related aim. Avoid reviews because it's hard to critique their strengths/weaknesses; cite reviews elsewhere only if necessary for other purposes (e.g., Innovation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and critique of preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary data should underpin conceptual and technical feasibility and must be presented with a discussion of their strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be selective; present data produced with the same rigor and transparency you propose. For datasets with weaknesses, explicitly acknowledge them and propose mitigation. The workbook suggests categorizing weaknesses: Severe (e.g., wrong cell line) — repeat before submission; Moderate (design flaws) — fix before R01 or submit smaller R03 to extend/repair; Minor — include with mitigation plan (e.g., imbalance in sexes, include mitigation text and future correction plan). After each dataset, include a sentence explaining how it supports the working hypothesis or feasibility of the aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach subsection format (per specific aim)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each Specific Aim, the Approach subsection should include: Introductory Paragraph; Research Design; Expected Outcomes; Potential Problems & Alternative Strategies; Timeline; Future Directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because literature and preliminary studies have been moved to Significance, the Approach per aim "collapses" to focus on design and execution. In Research Design explicitly address rigorous experimental design, relevant biological variables, and how key resources will be authenticated (authentication attachment references). Include expected outcomes and contingency/alternative approaches. Provide a timeline and optional future directions. Use clear, reviewer‑friendly organization and avoid repeating literature presented under Significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Design specifics to address reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Design must explicitly address the NIH foci of rigorous design and relevant biological variables, and describe how experiments will be implemented to reduce bias and increase robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details on sample size estimation (power analysis), randomization procedures, blinding, data collection and handling, statistical analysis plans, and measures to control biological variation. Describe GLP‑like practices where appropriate (SOPs, standardized recordkeeping), and indicate any fee‑for‑service or external evaluation resources if used. If statistical or design experts will be involved, name them or note their role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication attachment location and naming requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Between January 25 and May 24, 2016, authentication procedures must be uploaded as a separate one‑page PDF titled "Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources" into the R&R Other Project Information Other Attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include authentication details in Research Strategy (to avoid encroaching on page limits). The attachment must be ≤1 page and succinct. If following a recognized standard for authentication, cite it. The attachment should give enough procedural detail to show transparency (how reagents are obtained, tested, maintained), but not exhaustive protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer questions and scoring implications for new foci
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will be asked at least three questions and to provide comments about: (1) scientific premise, (2) rigorous experimental design / robust unbiased approaches, and (3) consideration of relevant biological variables; answers will contribute to Overall Impact score. Authentication will be rated Acceptable/Unacceptable (comment only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect reviewers to explicitly evaluate how you addressed each of these foci and incorporate their assessments into SIGNIFICANCE and APPROACH scoring. Authentication concerns labeled Unacceptable must be addressed before award. NIH may provide updated guidance for reviewers on public CSR pages; familiarize yourself with those reviewer resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgets must reflect costs of increased rigor and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing NIH’s changes may increase costs (larger subject numbers for sex‑disaggregated analyses, authentication testing, minor equipment, fee‑for‑service, external evaluators), and these must be budgeted appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop an internal breakout budget including new/one‑time costs. For Modular budgets, added costs may push you to the next module; if first year costs are higher (e.g., equipment), include Additional Narrative Justification. For R&R Breakout budgets, itemize costs and explain them in Budget Justification. Subcontractors must also reflect implementation costs and, if using Modular approach, subcontract costs are included in total direct costs and explained in Consortium Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects: change in definition of 'child'
rubrics_metrics.description: As of January 25, 2016, NIH defines a 'child' as anyone under the age of 18 (previously <21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update Human Subjects sections, consent/assent descriptions, and inclusion/age justification to reflect the new age cutoff to align with FOA and policy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals Section changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Eased descriptive requirements in the Vertebrate Animals section: veterinary care description no longer required; the number of animals is still required but justification has been moved to the Approach subsection; euthanasia method description is only required if it departs from AVMA guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the VAS checklist and include the numeric animal counts in the VAS section; provide justification of numbers and statistical rationale in the Approach Research Design. Follow VAS guidance (OLAW) and the FAQs for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to follow Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopting GLP‑like practices (planning, performance, monitoring, recording, reporting, archiving) is recommended to support reproducibility and reviewer confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement as many GLP principles as practical: standardized recordkeeping, SOPs, equipment maintenance/calibration, reagent dating/storage, validated assays, and training. Mentioning applicable GLP principles in the application signals seriousness about reproducibility. Cite GLP manuals/guidance if used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission review and writing schedule tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested pre‑submission timetable and tasks to maximize quality, including setting up a Pre‑Submission Review Committee, drafting Specific Aims early, iterative review and refinement, completing key forms, and institutional submission steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the workbook’s recommended checklist (notify program officer, send finalized Specific Aims and Innovation subsection to reviewers and PO, prepare Significance and Bibliography, prepare Cover Letter and Letters of Support, prepare Approach sections for each aim, develop biosketches and budget, assemble draft, send to Sponsored Programs 3–5 working days prior to deadline, and submit ≥1 day before agency deadline). Use the Pre‑Submission Review Committee to get constructive criticism and revise accordingly.
